stories.body: Houthi missile and drone attacks struck civilian, economic and energy sites in southern Saudi Arabia, wounding at least 73 people and starting fires that temporarily halted some operations, Saudi authorities said. The Houthis said the operation responded to more than 120 Saudi strikes in Yemen over the previous three days. The attacks come as Yemen’s Saudi-backed government launches a counteroffensive against the Iran-backed group, with fighting spreading across several fronts and officials pledging to retake Sanaa.
stories.headline: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia wound at least 73 and disrupt oil facilities

stories.body: Canada’s new retaliatory tariffs, ranging from 15% to 50% on about C$28 billion in US imports, took effect Tuesday in response to Washington’s 50% tariffs on Canadian goods. The measures cover sectors including steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, and electronics, though fresh fish and lobster were removed after industry objections. With negotiations stalled, President Donald Trump also threatened to block US sales by Canadian aircraft maker Bombardier unless it moves manufacturing to the United States.
stories.headline: Canada’s retaliatory tariffs on US goods take effect as Trump targets Bombardier

stories.body: Alternative for Germany won about 44% of the vote in Saxony-Anhalt, its strongest result in the eastern state but three seats short of an outright majority in the 83-seat parliament. The party is seeking partners or individual supporters to form a government, though mainstream parties have maintained their refusal to cooperate with it. The result would put a far-right party within reach of governing a German state for the first time since the Second World War and dealt a major blow to Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s CDU, which took about 17% of the vote.
stories.headline: Germany’s far-right AfD wins historic Saxony-Anhalt election victory

stories.body: Russia launched a major air attack on Kyiv after a three-day halt in strikes on the two countries’ capitals expired, killing at least two people and wounding 10, according to the city’s mayor. Ukraine said it downed 142 drones, 31 cruise missiles and two ballistic missiles, while damage was reported across several districts and in areas outside the capital. The pause had coincided with visits by US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to Moscow and Kyiv, but their talks produced no tangible breakthrough toward ending the war.
stories.headline: Russian strikes on Kyiv resume after three-day pause, killing at least two

stories.body: The UK is expected to impose a ban on trade in goods and some services from illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, part of a broader reset of its approach to Israel and the Palestinian cause. Separately, Britain committed £100 million to Ukraine’s air defences for the winter, including Patriot missiles, artillery ammunition and drones supplied through NATO’s Ukraine requirements mechanism. The aid comes as Ukraine faces continued Russian strikes and dwindling stocks of Patriot interceptors.
stories.headline: UK moves toward settlement trade sanctions and commits £100m for Ukraine air defence

stories.body: The International Atomic Energy Agency said it remains unable to verify Iran’s declared nuclear material or inspect key facilities more than a year after losing access, describing the situation as an urgent proliferation concern. France, Germany, the UK and the US are seeking support for an IAEA board resolution that would refer Iran’s case to the UN Security Council for the first time in two decades. Tehran says its programme is peaceful and has warned it will take necessary measures if the proposal advances, while US officials have acknowledged that a nuclear agreement may not be reachable.
stories.headline: IAEA warns over access to Iran’s nuclear programme as Western powers seek UN referral

stories.body: At least five people were killed after an Amazon cargo plane overran a runway at Miami International Airport, struck multiple vehicles and caught fire. The crash forced the closure of all runways at one of the country’s busiest airports. The National Transportation Safety Board said its investigation will examine airport safety systems as well as the circumstances of the aircraft’s collision with two vehicles.
stories.headline: Five killed after Amazon cargo plane overruns Miami airport runway

stories.body: The criminal case against ICE agent Christian Castro is an unusual instance of accountability during President Donald Trump’s second term, according to reporting by The Washington Post. The case stands out against a broader Justice Department pullback from investigating shootings by ICE agents involving protesters and other civilians, leaving agents facing limited consequences in many incidents.
stories.headline: Rare prosecution of ICE agent highlights Justice Department retreat from shooting investigations

stories.body: The latest OECD PISA assessment found a broad international decline in teenagers’ reading skills, with the United States trailing the UK and several other major education systems. The 2025 tests, taken by 760,000 15-year-olds in 91 countries, found that the share of students who rush through texts and give quick, incorrect answers has nearly doubled since 2018. OECD officials warned that the ability to critically evaluate complex information is deteriorating at a time when it is increasingly important.
stories.headline: US reading scores fall sharply in latest PISA assessment

stories.body: US gasoline averaged about $4.14 a gallon before Labor Day, the highest price ever recorded for the holiday and nearly a dollar above a year earlier, while diesel reached a record average of $5.85 a gallon. The increases have been driven by disruption to oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz during the war with Iran, alongside refinery problems. High fuel costs, persistent inflation and weak hiring have added to pressure on President Donald Trump’s economic promises even after an unexpectedly solid August jobs report.
stories.headline: Record Labor Day fuel prices intensify pressure on Trump over affordability

stories.body: Spain’s cabinet is declassifying intelligence, police and security reports produced between July 1 and August 1 concerning the mass entry of migrants into Ceuta on July 30 and 31. The National Court is investigating whether the events, which involved an estimated 70,000 arrivals in 24 hours, constituted a serious attack on Spain’s territorial integrity, including possible criminal organization and negligent homicide offences. The government says it will join the case as an injured party while maintaining that no intelligence service anticipated the mass crossing.
stories.headline: Spain declassifies reports on mass migrant entry into Ceuta

stories.body: Spain posted its worst results since 2000 in the OECD’s PISA assessment, falling below both OECD and EU averages in mathematics, reading and science. Compared with 2022, reading scores fell by 23 points, roughly more than a school year, mathematics dropped 16 points and science declined by eight. The decline was especially pronounced in reading, where only 2% of Spanish students reached the highest proficiency level, while the OECD linked a worldwide drop in complex reading ability partly to hurried digital reading and increased use of screens and AI tools.
stories.headline: Spain records historic decline in PISA performance

stories.body: Judge Juan Carlos Peinado summoned Begoña Gómez, the wife of Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, to a preliminary hearing that is required before a possible trial by jury on allegations including influence peddling and embezzlement. Gómez’s lawyer requested a postponement, saying the notice was too short and he had a prior professional commitment; the judge said he could reschedule if lawyers considered their attendance essential. The hearing is complicated by Peinado’s planned leave and impending retirement later this month.
stories.headline: Judge summons Begoña Gómez to preliminary hearing before possible trial

stories.body: Teachers launched a strike across Catalunya on the first day of the 2026-27 school year, blocking roads near Barcelona and in other areas before holding demonstrations and assemblies. Unions are demanding greater investment in public education, more staff, smaller class sizes, improved support for students with additional needs and better working conditions. The regional education department put early participation at 2.01%, though that figure was based on reports from only about one-fifth of public schools, while unions said they would continue mobilizing without progress in negotiations.
stories.headline: Teachers’ strike disrupts roads and classrooms on first day of school in Catalunya

stories.body: The OECD said Catalonia’s 2025 PISA results cannot be used for comparisons because 23.2% of selected students were excluded from testing, far above the 5% limit intended to preserve a representative sample. Spain’s education ministry nevertheless published the regional results, which appear above Spanish and OECD averages but are likely inflated because many students with learning, language, cognitive, behavioral or emotional difficulties were left out. Officials said an error in interpreting and transmitting testing guidance led to the exclusions, and the episode prompted the dismissal of a senior regional education official.
stories.headline: Catalonia’s PISA results cannot be compared after excessive student exclusions

stories.body: Barcelona is expected to remain hot and humid Tuesday, with temperatures reaching 31 to 33C, before an Atlantic front brings heavy rain, thunderstorms and a marked cooldown from overnight into Wednesday. Meteocat has issued warnings for intense rainfall, with some forecasts suggesting more than 40 millimeters could fall in 30 minutes and localized totals potentially reaching 60 millimeters in three hours. The change will end an exceptional early-September heatwave and could lower temperatures by 10C or more.
stories.headline: Heavy rain and thunderstorms expected in Barcelona after exceptional heatwave
